notes: Open slot used: gwely (bed), CorCenCC rank 707, because Cai is in bed for most of the chapter and no planned lexeme means 'bed'. It is declared in learning_contract.open_slot_ids and in the gwely entry's notes in lexicon-deltas/pennod-19.json; the integrator should add it to chapters.json open_slot_words for Pennod 19.

All seven conjugated forms of ar are used in story sentences (arna i, arnat ti, arno fe, arni hi, arnon ni, arnoch chi, arnyn nhw); the literal 'Mae tair blanced arno fe' sits beside the idiom 'Mae gwres arno fe' as the chapter's contrast, and gyda (possession) is contrasted in Pensum A. Pen tost takes gyda, not ar (southern Mynediad: a named sore body part with gyda, conditions such as annwyd and peswch with ar), so s015 sets 'Mae pen tost gyda fi' beside 'mae syched arna i' as a second contrast inside the target.

Deliberate error: Dafi's 'Mae syched gyda fi!' is corrected by Mali in the next line ('Mae syched arnat ti: dim gyda ti, ond arnat ti!'), and Dafi repeats it correctly, contrasting this chapter's target with Pennod 8 gyda.
The illness follows its own snowy hunt (told in the past in the opening paragraph), so it does not depend on the autumn hunt of Pennod 16.
'Beth sy'n bod?' is used as the whitelisted formula (from 19) and glossed at first use.
Lexicon delta lists the conjugated forms under cy-ar with a 'conj' card stage (design §8.3).

primary_new_grammar.label: ar idioms of illness and feeling (Mae annwyd / gwres / peswch / ofn / syched / cywilydd / angen … ar …) with the conjugated forms arna i, arnat ti, arno fe, arni hi, arnon ni, arnoch chi, arnyn nhw; contrast with gyda (possession, and the southern sore-body-part construction Mae pen tost gyda fi) and literal ar (on)

cover.alt: Cai lies ill in his box bed under three blankets; Elen sits beside him with her hand on his forehead, Myrddin pours red medicine from a small glass jug into a spoon, and Arth sits at the bedside, worried.
cover.art_brief: A small timber sleeping room in the llys on a winter morning, light through a shuttered unglazed window (llys palette: warm wood, limewash, thatch; snow outside). Cai (15, tall, red-blond, square-jawed) lies in a wooden box bed under three woollen blankets, cheeks flushed, hair damp with sweat, miserable. Elen (about fifty, white linen veil, forest-green dress, iron key-ring) sits on the bed edge, one hand on his forehead. Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat) pours bright red syrup from a small glass jug with a handle (prose s041: "jwg bach") into a wooden spoon held out to Cai; the neat little glass jug looks out of place. Arth (11, untidy brown hair with cowlick, moss-green tunic) sits on a low chair at the bedside, worried. Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) peers in from the doorway. A cup of water and a bowl of cawl on a stool. No text.

grammar.nodyn_en: Welsh puts a cold, fever, fear or thirst 'on' you: Mae annwyd ar Cai 'Cai has a cold', Mae ofn arna i 'I'm afraid'. With pronouns: arna i, arnat ti, arno fe, arni hi, arnon ni, arnoch chi, arnyn nhw. Need: Mae angen help arna i. A sore body part takes gyda, like possession: Mae pen tost gyda fi.
